question: The Election Commission of India became a three-member body in 1989, again it was made into a single member body in the year _________ .
solution:
The correct answer is __**1990**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Election Commission of India was initially established as a single-member body.
 
• In 1989, the Election Commission was expanded to a three-member body to handle the increased workload and responsibilities.
 
• However, this three-member structure was reverted back to a single-member body in 1990.
 
• The change back to a single-member body was part of a process to streamline the decision-making process within the commission.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Election Commission of India (ECI):**

 
 
• The Election Commission of India is an autonomous constitutional authority responsible for administering election processes in India at national and state levels.
 
• The body administers elections to the Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha, and State Legislative Assemblies, as well as the offices of the President and Vice President in the country.
 
• The ECI was established on January 25, 1950.
 
• Initially, the commission had only a Chief Election Commissioner. Two additional Commissioners were appointed for the first time on October 16, 1989, but they had a very short tenure until January 1, 1990.
 
 
 
• **Chief Election Commissioner (CEC):**
 
 
• The Chief Election Commissioner heads the Election Commission of India.
 
• The CEC has tenure of six years, or up to the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
 
• The CEC can be removed from office only through impeachment by Parliament.
 
• The Chief Election Commissioner and the two Election Commissioners enjoy the same decision-making powers.
 
 
 
• **Election Commissioners:**
 
 
• They assist the Chief Election Commissioner in the discharge of his/her duties.
 
• The President of India appoints the Election Commissioners.
 
• They hold office for a term of six years or until they attain the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.
 
 
 
• **Article 324:**
 
 
• Article 324 of the Constitution of India provides for the appointment of the Chief Election Commissioner and Election Commissioners.
 
• It vests the power of superintendence, direction, and control of elections in the Election Commission.
 
• The article ensures the independence and impartiality of the Election Commission.
